title: Are Zeus and Jupiter the same god? In myth, yes. In Rome, no.
cover:
Zeus = Jupiter?
In myth, yes.
In Rome, no.

scenes.text: Are Zeus and Jupiter the same god? In myth, yes. In Rome, no.
Ovid tells the stories of Zeus under Latin names: the son of Saturn, the thunderbolt controller.
Birth, thunderbolt, kingship, love affairs: it's Hesiod and Homer in Roman dress.
And the name only travels one way: Greek texts never call Zeus Jupiter.
But in cult, he's a different god. Rome's first temple was his: Jupiter Feretrius, where Romulus hung the spoils of the king he killed.
As his army flees, Romulus vows him another temple: Jupiter Stator, the Stayer.
And in Virgil, Jupiter promises Rome an empire without end.
Hesiod's Zeus rules because the gods asked him to. And he promises no city anything.
Rule of thumb: in the stories, Jupiter is the Roman Zeus. In religion, he's the god of Rome.
Which text says so? Ovid and Hesiod for the myth; Livy and Virgil for Rome.
Save it, and send it to anyone who says Jupiter is just Zeus with a new name.
